answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit deletion bond in the juniper registry and files key-signed deletion certificates in the glacier archive. A terrace auditor audits 5% each epoch by re-querying the data holder; a missing or reused certificate burns the bond. Each fake pays 70 bond plus 30 audit fee, so the kth fake still pays 100 and 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits, since each certificate binds one key to one store and cannot be reused. A rented-deletion ring fails: rented certificates carry the renter key, so the terrace check rejects them. An honest identity pays once.
